title: Harvest schedule and rollback oven notes - Nov 2026 (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working canvas for the November harvest window. Mix of schedule, lightweight gating criteria, and a compact rollback 'oven' (practical steps that operators can run when a hot rollback is needed). Intention: ship a modest model/infra tweak with low overhead, and have a fast, rehearsed rollback path.

High level runway (two-week mini-window):
- Nov 16: Code freeze for this roll (no new infra changes).
- Nov 17–18: Canary day 1 (5% traffic for canary-variant A).
- Nov 19: Canary day 2 (15% traffic if day 1 all green).
- Nov 20–22: Staggered ramp to 50% with hourly sampling and sentinel checks.
- Nov 23: Quiet window — no further config changes; extended monitoring.
- Nov 24: Final decision — promote or revert.

Calendar quick matrix (human-readable):
Date | Window | Action | Lead
Nov 16 | freeze -> prep | gate checklist run, smoke tests | Maya
Nov 17 | canary-1 05% | enable routing rule canary-A; 2h stationary | Ethan
Nov 18 | observe | metrics pass? decide ramp | Priya
Nov 19 | canary-2 15% | ramp to 15% if sanity OK | Maya
Nov 20-22 | ramp | hourly sampling + trace diff | Liam
Nov 23 | quiet | telemetry bake | SRE oncall
Nov 24 | decision | promote / rollback | Release lead

Gating criteria (must be explicitly OK before each ramp):
- Latency: p50 and p95 for core generation endpoint must not regress > 10% relative to baseline. Absolute thresholds: p95 < 450ms target for region-us-west.
- Errors: 5xx rate < 0.5% (sustained over 10m).
- Quality signal: embedding cosine drift < 0.02 on sampled prompts (eval harness).
- Cost: per-token spend change < +12% (early alert if spike).
- User-facing anomalies: any spike in NLU fallback or increased hallucination reports -> immediate hold.

Telemetry and quick-check scripts (operators):
- Canary health: /scripts/check_canary_health.sh --canary canary-A --window 15m (returns PASS/FAIL and a short json).
- Trace diff: /scripts/trace_diff.py --baseline baseline-2026-11-01 --candidate canary-A --top 50
- Smoke: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.local/v1/generate -d '@smoke-sample.json' | jq '.status,.latency'

Alert thresholds (on-call):
- pager duty if 5xx rate > 0.8% for 5m OR p95 > 750ms for 3m.
- Slack #release-ops mention with @oncall if embedding drift > 0.05 on sample set.

Rollback oven (fast path) — a compact checklist that an operator can run from the console in order. Keep these commands ready in a pinned GH gist.
1) Abort ramp and flip routing to baseline variant (stateless routing):
   - curl -X POST https://console.redwood.local/api/routing -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY' -d '{"route":"/generate","variant":"baseline"}'
   - Confirm traffic: /scripts/confirm_route.sh --expected baseline --tolerance 2%
2) If rollout was via infra config (k8s / svc selector), fall back to the previous deployment:
   - kubectl -n serving rollout undo deployment/serving-canary-A --to-revision=$(kubectl -n serving rollout history deployment/serving-canary-A | head -n 1 | awk '{print $1}')
   - watch kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=serving | grep Terminating -v
3) Hotfix patch (if revert not possible and small fix exists):
   - cherry-pick PR branch: git fetch origin && git checkout -b hotfix/revert-1097 origin/main && git cherry-pick <sha-of-fix>
   - run localized smoke: ./local-smoke.sh
   - create PR with emergency label and request fast-review (two approvers)
4) Post-rollback validation: run the same smoke and trace-diff scripts, confirm p95/p50 within baseline tolerance, and send the rollback notice.

Communications (short template):
- When initiating canary: "Starting Canary A (5%) for harvest window. Owning leads: Maya, Ethan. Slate pinned in #release-ops. Canary-id: harvest-A-20261117"
- If holding: "Holding ramp: see telemetry slices #release-ops. Reason: {brief reason}. Owners: {names}. Action: investigate {hypothesis}."
- If rollback: "Rollback executed at {time UTC}. Steps: routing flip + deploy undo. Incident ticket: JIRA-4821. Postmortem owner: Priya."

Preflight checklist (before Nov 16 freeze):
- [ ] Merge release branch and tag with semantic release (release/harvest-2026-11-16).
- [ ] Nightly infra tests green (last 48h).
- [ ] Canary harness updated with new eval prompts (file: /eval/harvest-2026/sample-set.json).
- [ ] Ops playbook pinned in #release-ops and on-call briefed.
- [ ] A/B feature flags audited; ensure kill-switch flag available for immediate flip.

Lightweight release notes (draft):
- What: small serving runtime optimization and model quantization adjustment to reduce token compute.
- Why: reduce variance in tail latency and lower average per-token cost for long-context workloads.
- Risk: potential minor change in embedding drift for some edge prompts — mitigated by limited canary and embedding checks.
- Rollout plan: staged canary Nov 17–24 as described.
- Rollback path: routing flip + deployment undo.
- Contacts: Maya Chen (release lead), Ethan Rivera (canary operator), Priya Nair (postmortem owner), SRE oncall.

Open questions / action items:
- [ ] Confirm whether third-party loadgen will hit the canary in eu-west (regional routing is still being validated). (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Add one more synthetic prompt aimed at long-context hallucination checks. (owner: Research/AppliedML)
- [ ] Who will own the customer comms if we need an external-facing incident note? (owner: Customer Success lead)

Quick retro anchors to capture post-rollout (short-notes):
- Signal clarity: which single metric told us to hold? Could we simplify?
- Runbook noise: which steps felt ambiguous? Add exact commands + expected outputs.
- Handoff: was shift rotation sufficient? Improve shift checklist if not.

Notes to self (Maya):
- Keep the 'oven' commands under 10 steps; practice once in a dry-run this week.
- Pin the eval harness runbook to the Gist and ensure permissions for SRE.

End of doc - this is intentionally compact so operators can print/paste commands. Treat as living; update as we rehearse the oven.
